GOOGLEDRIVE_FILE_CREATED_TRIGGER.name: File Created
GOOGLEDRIVE_FILE_CREATED_TRIGGER.description: Triggers when a new file is created in Google Drive.
GOOGLEDRIVE_FILE_CREATED_TRIGGER.instructions:
Instructions for setting up the trigger:

    - This trigger monitors Google Drive for newly created files.
    - You can optionally provide a search query to filter which files to monitor.
    - You can optionally limit monitoring to a specific parent folder by ID.
    - On the first run the trigger baselines to the current time and emits no
      past events.
    - Subsequent polls return files created since the previous poll.
    - The cursor is provider-derived from `file.createdTime`, not local wall
      clock — clock skew between the poller and Google does not affect it.

NOTION_PAGE_CREATED.name: Page Created
NOTION_PAGE_CREATED.description:
Triggers when a new Notion page is created.

    Customer optionally scopes with at most one of:
      - data_source_id: new row in this data source
      - parent_page_id: new sub-page under this page (immediate parent only)

    With neither set, fires for any new page in the workspace the
    integration has access to. Notion sends ~60s aggregation latency on
    most events.
NOTION_PAGE_CREATED.instructions:
**Setting Up the Trigger**

    1. Create a webhook subscription on your Notion public integration.
    2. Use `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/trigger_instances/notion/pr_gfaBXClV3lSG/handle` as the webhook URL.
    3. Notion sends a one-time verification request containing a
       `verification_token`. Composio captures it automatically.
    4. Retrieve the captured verification token from Composio and paste it
       into Notion's "Verify Subscription" UI to activate the subscription.
    5. Subscribe the integration to the event categories the trigger needs
       (Page, Data source, View, Comment, etc.).

`type` is one of: `database`, `page`, `team`, `workspace`, or
occasionally `data_source` for the post-2025-09-03 API. Different
parent shapes apply to different event types — see each trigger's
description for what to expect.

SLACK_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.name: Channel Message Received
SLACK_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.description:
Triggered when a message is posted in a Slack channel
    (public, private, or multi-party IM). Does NOT match direct messages.
SLACK_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.instructions: To use this trigger, ensure your Slack app has the `channels:history`, `groups:history`, and `mpim:history` OAuth scopes.

channel_id.description: Specific channel to watch. Null = all channels.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

channel_type.description: Filter by channel type. channel = public, group = private, mpim = multi-party IM. Null = all types.
channel_type.title: Channel Type

is_bot_message.description: Filter by message source. true = only bot messages, false = only human messages, null = all.
is_bot_message.title: Is Bot Message

is_thread_reply.description: Filter by thread status. true = only thread replies, false = only top-level, null = all.
is_thread_reply.title: Is Thread Reply

SLACK_DIRECT_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.name: Direct Message Received
SLACK_DIRECT_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.description:
Triggered when a new direct message (DM) is sent to a user in Slack.
    Catches all DMs across all DM channels.
SLACK_DIRECT_MESSAGE_RECEIVED.instructions: To use this trigger, ensure your Slack app has the `im:history` OAuth scope.

attachments.description: Attachments included with the direct message, if any. Some Slack apps (like Datadog) send content via attachments rather than the top-level text field.
attachments.title: Attachments

bot_id.description: The ID of the bot that sent the direct message
bot_id.title: Bot Id

channel.description: The ID of the direct message channel
channel.title: Channel

channel_type.description: The type of the channel (should be 'im' for direct messages)
channel_type.title: Channel Type

files.description: Files uploaded with the direct message, if any. Present when subtype is 'file_share'. Contains file metadata including name, mimetype, and URLs.
files.title: Files

team_id.description: The ID of the team where the direct message was sent
team_id.title: Team Id

text.description: The text content of the direct message
text.title: Text

ts.description: The timestamp of the direct message
ts.title: Ts

user.description: The ID of the user who sent the direct message
user.title: User
